name: REDORZO TOP CALENDAR — Booking System for Appointments, Rentals & Events
author: REDORZO

sections.description:
A free booking calendar and online reservation system for every trade that takes bookings: tours and outings, classes, appointments, rentals, stays, workshops, events and restaurant tables. Your customers book online from their phone in a few taps; you run the day from one clear screen.

REDORZO TOP CALENDAR is a complete booking system for WordPress: appointment scheduling, class and event booking, tour and activity booking, holiday rental and B&B reservations, restaurant table reservations, and bike, boat or equipment rental. Customers pick a day, a time and how many people, and receive a confirmation with a private link to manage their booking — no account, no password. You see what needs your attention today, move a booking by dragging it, and take a booking on the phone in seconds.

Every booking is checked on your server before it is saved: the same place, room or table is never sold twice, even when two customers click at the same moment.

Works with block themes and classic themes: the booking form sits inside your theme, with your header, menus and footer, in light or dark colours. Your customers’ data stays on your site.

Free, with no limit on activities, dates, places or bookings, and no time limit. Online payment, equipment and reports come with TOP CALENDAR Plus, a separate extension (see below).

Made for your trade

The first time you open it, a short welcome screen asks what you do, your opening hours and your first activity. Every screen then speaks your trade:

  • Outings and activities (tour booking): guides, clubs, water sports centres, adventure parks.
  • Appointments (appointment scheduling): practices, salons, studios, consultants.
  • Stays (holiday rental and B&B booking): holiday cottages, B&Bs, campsites, booked by the night.
  • Classes (class booking): yoga, dance, music, sport.
  • Workshops and events (event booking): tastings, talks, courses.
  • Tables (restaurant reservations): restaurants, bars, wine cellars, counted in covers.
  • Rentals (bike, boat and equipment rental): bikes, boats, vehicles, equipment. Each rental names what it rents, so customers read “6 bikes left” and “How many bikes?”.
  • Something else: neutral words, which can be changed later.

A booking form made for phones

  • Five short steps: what, how many, who, payment, done. Going back or refreshing never loses what was typed, with or without JavaScript.
  • A strip of days shows at a glance which dates are open or full, and every time slot says how many places are left.
  • A full date is never a dead end: the nearest open dates come first, then the waiting list.
  • Every button can be tapped with a thumb, every text can be read, in light and dark.
  • A booking page is created for you; a block and a shortcode place the calendar on any page, in five views: list, month, day, year and cards.
  • A booking can last an hour, a day, or several nights.

Customers manage their own booking

The confirmation email carries a private link. From that page, a customer sees the booking, moves it to another date, changes the number of people, adds it to their calendar, or cancels it while your rules allow it. Emails read well on a phone and in dark mode, go out in the language of the booking, and “Reply” reaches you.

A waiting list that fills the gaps

When a date is full, visitors join the waiting list and say how many places they need. When a place frees up, “Offer a place” writes to the next person in one click.

A console built around today

  • Today: what needs your attention, who still has to pay, the day hour by hour, and tomorrow already.
  • Planning by month, week, day and agenda. Drag a booking to move it: the screen says what the move frees and what it takes before anything is saved.
  • New booking: take a booking on the phone or at the counter, with the places left shown as you type.
  • Requests: the bookings that wait for your answer, and how long each one still holds its place.
  • Close a morning, an afternoon or a whole day, and see first which bookings it affects.
  • Search by name, email or booking reference, from every screen.
  • Customer files, staff with their colour and time off, four team roles, a history for every booking and a Journal of every change.
  • Write to a customer from the console: the email leaves from your site and is noted in the booking history.

Prices, and payment on the day

Put a price on any activity, with prices by season, paid options and discount codes. Customers see the total before they book, and what is left to pay on the day. At the desk, record cash, card terminal, cheque or bank transfer, as a deposit or in full. The payment receipt can carry a numbered PDF invoice, made on your own server.

Calendar sync, import and export

  • Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar through iCal: a private feed of your schedule to subscribe to, and private calendars read back so busy times close the dates on your site.
  • Import an existing agenda from an .ics file or a spreadsheet.
  • Export bookings, customers, the waiting list and departure lists to CSV, or everything at once.

Accessible, translated, yours

  • Booking form, customer page and console checked against WCAG 2.2 level AA, and usable with the keyboard alone.
  • Seven translations included: French, German, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Polish and Brazilian Portuguese.
  • A counter QR code that leads to your booking page, with a poster ready to print.
  • WordPress’s Export and Erase Personal Data tools cover your customers’ data.

What this plugin does not do

  • No online payment. Customers pay on the day, and you record the payment at the desk. Card payment and WooCommerce come with TOP CALENDAR Plus.
  • Nothing leaves your site. No account, no key, no tracking, no remote fonts or scripts. The only outside connection is the calendar sync, and only if you set it up.
  • No text messages. Confirmations, changes and cancellations go by email.

Want to take payment online?

TOP CALENDAR Plus, by REDORZO, is a separate, paid extension, sold at https://redorzo.com/top-calendar. It installs next to this plugin and adds:

  • online payment by card with Stripe, or through your WooCommerce checkout, with deposits and refunds;
  • a WooCommerce product page that sells a time slot of an activity;
  • equipment: rooms, vehicles, items for hire, named units with their upkeep and history, and a planning by equipment;
  • reports: bookings and takings week by week, how full each session ran, and a spreadsheet for your accountant;
  • the automatic reminder email before each booking.

You install it next to this plugin, and it brings its own screens. This plugin only describes it, under TOP CALENDAR → Settings → TOP CALENDAR Plus, with a link to that page. Removing Plus never deletes a booking, a customer or a setting.

External services

This plugin does not contact any service of its own. It never contacts redorzo.com: it has no key check and no update channel, and it is updated by WordPress.org like every other plugin in the directory.

Calendar sync is the only feature that reaches outside your site, and only when you set it up. If you paste the private iCal address of a calendar (for example Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar) under TOP CALENDAR → Settings → Calendars, the plugin downloads that address about every fifteen minutes to read its busy times. The request goes to the address you entered and carries nothing about your customers. The provider’s own terms and privacy policy apply, for example https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy for Google Calendar. Removing the address stops the requests.

The “Your calendar app” card in My account, and the private feeds of TOP CALENDAR → Settings → Calendars, offer buttons that open another site in the user’s browser, only when the user clicks them: “Add to Google Calendar” opens https://calendar.google.com, “Add to Outlook” opens https://outlook.live.com, and “Add to Outlook (work or school account)” opens https://outlook.office.com. “Add to Apple Calendar” opens the calendar app of the user’s own device and reaches no site. Each button carries the user’s private, read-only calendar link, so that Google or Microsoft can subscribe to it; that service then downloads the link from time to time to show the user’s bookings (first names and numbers of places only, or numbers of places alone if the user chose so). The plugin itself sends nothing to these services. Google: https://policies.google.com/terms and https://policies.google.com/privacy. Microsoft: https://www.microsoft.com/servicesagreement and https://privacy.microsoft.com/privacystatement. “Regenerate the link” stops every subscription made with the old one.

When the public calendar is on (it is on a new site, off on a site updated from an earlier version, and you choose under TOP CALENDAR → Settings → Calendars), your booking page shows visitors a “Subscribe to this calendar” box with the same kind of links: “Google Calendar” opens https://calendar.google.com, “Outlook” opens https://outlook.live.com, and “Apple Calendar” opens the calendar app of the visitor’s device. They open only when the visitor clicks them, and they carry the address of your public calendar: your upcoming dates, activity names, times, places and a link to book — never a customer. The same terms and privacy policies of Google and Microsoft apply. Switching the public calendar off removes the box and stops the feed.

The separate paid extension, TOP CALENDAR Plus, is not part of this plugin and declares its own services (Stripe, and its own update channel).

Privacy

The console’s fonts are bundled with the plugin. No administrator’s IP address reaches a third party when a screen is opened.

The plugin stores the personal data your customers give when they book: name, email address, phone number, and the address fields you choose to ask for. It plugs into WordPress’s own privacy tools, so Tools → Export Personal Data and Tools → Erase Personal Data cover TOP CALENDAR without any extra step.

Erasing does not delete bookings: it removes everything that identifies a person and keeps the date, the amount and the status, because a paid booking is an accounting record. The report returned to you says what was kept.

The figures on the “Your public page” screen are counters added up per day: visits, how many on a phone, bookings, the server’s response time and the time from the form to the booking. There is no cookie, no IP address and no identifier: the browser’s user agent is read on the spot (robot or not, phone or not) and not stored. Robots are not counted. The counters are kept 35 days, and “delete all data” on uninstall removes them.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “REDORZO TOP CALENDAR”, then click Install Now and Activate. You can also upload the zip file from Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Open the TOP CALENDAR menu. A short welcome screen asks for your trade, your opening hours and your first activity.
  3. A public Bookings page is created with the booking form. Add it to your menu, or place the TOP CALENDAR block or the [top_calendar] shortcode on any page.
  4. Print the counter QR code from the end of the welcome screen if you take walk-in customers.
sections.faq:
Is TOP CALENDAR really free?

Yes. The free plugin has no limit on activities, dates, places or bookings, and no time limit. Online payment, equipment, reports and the automatic reminder come with the paid TOP CALENDAR Plus extension.

Can I take payments online?

Not with the free plugin alone. Customers see the price and pay on the day, and the console records the payment. Online card payment with Stripe, or through WooCommerce, comes with TOP CALENDAR Plus.

Does it need WooCommerce?

No. WooCommerce is only used by TOP CALENDAR Plus, to take payments through your shop’s checkout and to sell a time slot from a product page.

Can I use it for appointments?

Yes. Choose “Appointment” on the welcome screen: an appointment is a booking for one person, and the screens then speak of sessions and patients. Staff can be given their own colour and time off.

Can customers book online from their phone?

Yes. The booking form is made for phones first: five short steps, every button within reach of a thumb, and a confirmation email with a private link to manage the booking. It works on a computer just as well.

Which businesses is it for?

Any business that takes bookings by date and time: tour guides and outdoor activity centres, practices and salons taking appointments, holiday cottages, B&Bs and campsites, yoga, dance and music classes, workshops and events, restaurants and bars, and bike, boat, vehicle or equipment rental.

Can I rent out rooms, cottages or equipment?

Yes. Choose “Stay” to book by the night (a two-night stay is charged two nights, and no night is sold twice), or “Rental” to count items instead of people. Each rental can name what it rents, in the singular and the plural (“bike” / “bikes”), and customers read it everywhere: “6 bikes left”, “How many bikes?”, “2 bikes” in their emails. Named units with their own maintenance record come with TOP CALENDAR Plus.

Does it work for restaurants?

Yes. Choose “Table”: bookings are counted in covers, by sitting.

Can customers change or cancel their booking?

Yes, from the private link in their emails, with no account. You decide until when cancelling online is allowed; after that, the page says how to get in touch.

Can I add the booking calendar to any page?

Yes. Use the TOP CALENDAR block in the editor, or the [top_calendar] shortcode. The booking shows inside your theme by default; full screen is a setting under TOP CALENDAR → Settings → General.

Does it sync with Google Calendar?

Yes, through iCal. Your schedule is published as a private feed that Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar can subscribe to, and the private iCal address of a personal calendar can be read back so its busy times close dates on your site.

Does it send reminders?

Booking confirmations, changes and cancellations are sent by the free plugin. The automatic reminder before the booking comes with TOP CALENDAR Plus.

Is it GDPR-friendly?

The plugin plugs into WordPress’s Export and Erase Personal Data tools and contacts no outside service of its own. Its cookies are first-party and short-lived: the language chosen on the booking form, the link to a place offered from the waiting list, and, for two hours, whether the visitor arrived through the counter QR code. Erasing keeps the date, amount and status of a paid booking, because it is an accounting record.

How do I delete a test booking?

Cancel it, then choose “Delete permanently” in its menu. To clear several, tick them in Bookings and click “Delete the cancelled ones”. A booking with an invoice or a payment record is kept as an accounting record, and the screen offers to anonymise the customer instead.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

By default, bookings, customers and settings are kept, so reinstalling finds everything where it was. Scheduled tasks, roles and temporary data are always removed. To remove everything, tick the option in the settings before deleting the plugin.

What happens if I remove TOP CALENDAR Plus?

Nothing is deleted: bookings, customers, prices and settings belong to this plugin, and reinstalling Plus finds them where they were.
sections.changelog:
1.2.5

  • “No recurrence” when you plan an activity: one date, one departure, and it is no longer offered once the date has passed. The activity editor has it too.
  • “Until” under “Exact dates…” now starts on the same day as “From”: typing only the day and the month no longer opens a whole year of dates.
  • “Prepare the next season” no longer brings back an activity that had a single date.
  • “Attendees”, in the menu of an activity, opens the list of one date: who is booked, who has arrived, what is left to take on site, the waiting list, an attendance sheet to print and the spreadsheet of that date. Undoing “Arrived” or “Absent” no longer emails the customer.
  • The “All activities” menu lists your main families only, in the calendar and now in “Our activities” too; your choice follows you from one view to the other.
  • Choosing a family or an activity in the calendar shows all its upcoming dates in one list (40 at a time, then “Show more dates”); “See month by month” brings the grid back. The “Families and their activities” menu option is gone.
  • Today: the money taken today is compared with last week at the same time of day, not with the whole day.
  • After the first booking from a customer, the Today screen asks once for a review on WordPress.org, in a card you can hide for good.
  • Once setup is done and a week has passed, administrators see one card presenting TOP CALENDAR Plus — on the Dashboard, the Plugins screen and the Today screen only. It goes away for good when dismissed, is not shown once TOP CALENDAR Plus is installed, and makes no network request.
  • A draft activity no longer shows on the public page through an old address.

1.2.4

  • A Families screen: rename a family, group families that look alike, file a family under another, and put the activities without a family away in one go.
  • Four new layouts for “Our activities”: by family, agenda, photo cards and compact list. A site updated from an earlier version keeps its page as it was until you change it.
  • Visitors can subscribe to your public calendar in Google, Apple or Outlook: your upcoming dates only, never a customer.
  • A full time slot shows “Full” in the list of times instead of disappearing.
  • “Back to WordPress” sits in the left menu, under Settings.
  • The console and the public page read better on a phone.

1.2.3

  • Same version number as TOP CALENDAR Plus 1.2.3. No change to the free plugin.

1.2.2

  • First release.

screenshots.caption: One plugin, every trade: pick your line of work and the console speaks it — Outings, Classes, Sessions, Rentals, Workshops or Sittings; Instructors, Teachers, Practitioners or Hosts; Customers, Members, Patients, Visitors or Diners.
The booking page: the next date first, the places left at every time, and booked from a phone in a few taps.
Today: what needs your attention, the day as it goes, and the day in three figures.
Planning: the month at a glance; press + on any day to open a session in a centred window, with just a name and the seats.

Your trade: eight lines of work to choose from — outings, appointments, rentals, stays, classes, workshops, tables or neutral words. It changes the words, never the engine, and can be changed at any time.
New booking: who, how many, what and when, typed in one go, with the places left and the total, all on one screen.
Customer page: a private link in every email to add the booking to a calendar, change it or write to you, with no account.
